arc: hook: the polish-vs-control tradeoff → ground the answer in one editable storyboard → build the agent pipeline that fills and audits it → peak: cinematic, trustworthy, and free at once → takeaway: your topic, rendered — planned, checked, free
viewer_question: Can I get a genuinely cinematic AI video without giving up control — or paying for it?

director_note.thesis: You never have to trade control for polish or pay for either — an agent pipeline writing one auditable, human-editable storyboard makes AI video creative, trustworthy, and free at the same time.
not: no feature-by-feature tour of the skill
no fabricated benchmarks, speeds, costs, or timings — the brief gives none
no comparison against a named competitor product
no how-to / tutorial steps — this is a launch film, not a walkthrough

anti_slop: every beat states only what its source_ref in the brief supports — no claim without a trace
no invented numbers, benchmarks, render times, or dollar figures; the brief has none, so stay qualitative
don't overclaim the tradeoff: the brief never says competitors cost money — frame 'free' as THIS tool's property, not a jab at others
no fact carried by a decorative photoreal image — facts stay as on-screen text/UI; broll is accompaniment only, never the carrier of a claim
rhythm: calm hero hook (7s) → two quick build beats (9s each) → a longer slow-burn climax (11s, peak) → a sparse 6s hold
assumed_known: what a JSON / config file is, and that it is plain text a developer can open and edit
neural text-to-speech / voiceover as a concept
the general idea of AI video generators (the category this tool competes in)
command-line rendering tools like ffmpeg, loosely

beats.learning_point: AI video forces a tradeoff: hand over control to get polish, or keep control and get something rough.
beats.source_ref: brief: why_it_matters ('Most AI video tools trade control for polish or polish for control')
beats.narration_intent: Lead with the tension as a hero line: AI video makes you choose — surrender control to get something polished, or keep control and get something rough. Pose the open question the film will answer (can you have both — and what does it cost you?). Do NOT say the product's name yet; withhold the resolution.
beats.continuity: inherits: — (cold open) · hooks: names a real, unresolved tension (control vs polish) and withholds whether both are possible — pulls the viewer into 'so how?'

beats.learning_point: The whole video is one thing you can read and edit — a storyboard.json — and an agent pipeline writes it.
beats.source_ref: brief: mechanism (storyboard.json single source of truth; content-planner, design-director, scriptwriter, critic panel) + why_it_matters ('human-editable storyboard')
beats.narration_intent: Answer 'how do you keep control?' first: the entire video lives in one storyboard.json you can open and edit — the single source of truth (anchor on the familiar 'a plain text file you own'). Then name the four pipeline stages in spoken order, each with a distinct phrase: content-planner decides WHAT each beat teaches; design-director decides HOW it looks; scriptwriter writes the NARRATION; a critic panel AUDITS the result.
beats.continuity: inherits: the open 'can you keep control?' tension from the hook · hooks: you can edit the storyboard — but agents made the creative calls, so can you trust them, and what does it cost?

beats.learning_point: Those creative choices are trustworthy and free: deterministic gates audit every render, and nothing needs a paid API key.
beats.source_ref: brief: evidence[2] (validate, keyframe_qa, rhythm_qa, check_av gate every render) + evidence[0] (free by default — edge-tts, ffmpeg, PIL, no paid key)
beats.narration_intent: Lead with trust: before every render, deterministic gates audit that storyboard — sweep them as one phrase, 'deterministic checks' (structure and captions, visual QA, pacing, audio/video drift). Then the second, distinct point: it all runs FREE by default — neural voice from edge-tts, ffmpeg, PIL captions, no paid API key. Two parallel guarantees, two phrases: 'checked' and 'free.'
beats.continuity: inherits: an agent pipeline wrote the storyboard · hooks: it's audited and it's free — but is the OUTPUT actually good enough to matter? → the cinematic payoff

beats.learning_point: So the tradeoff is false: the result is a truly cinematic video that is creative, trustworthy, AND free — from a storyboard you still control.
beats.source_ref: brief: evidence[3] (cinematic tier — camera over 3D depth planes, bold templates re-skinned from one accent, native components) + thesis ('both creative and trustworthy')
beats.narration_intent: The payoff that resolves the hook — you never had to trade. Lead with the result: a genuinely CINEMATIC video, a camera gliding over 3D depth planes, bold templates re-skinned from one accent. Then land the synthesis in one breath: creative AND trustworthy AND free — all from a storyboard you still control. This is the peak; let it breathe. Do not stack extra features here.
beats.continuity: inherits: it's audited and free · hooks: the output is cinematic — which resolves the whole control-vs-polish tension the film opened on (payoff)

beats.learning_point: A topic becomes a narrated, designed video — agent-planned, deterministically checked, free by default.
beats.narration_intent: One sparse line that answers the opening question and nothing more: a topic becomes a narrated, designed video — agent-planned, deterministically checked, free by default.
beats.continuity: inherits: the tradeoff is false · hooks: — (close) — restates the one thing as the takeaway the viewer leaves with
